summary: This benchmark evaluates cross-model activation surgery by mapping two separate operand representations from a 7B donor model into a frozen 14B host model during basic arithmetic execution. The evaluation demonstrates 100% composition accuracy across 512 addition and subtraction program groups against rigorous negative and positive controls. While the task scope is narrow and synthetically constrained to single-digit arithmetic, the experimental methodology and parameter specification are sound.
strengths: Rigorous experimental controls, including norm-matched random injection (0% success) and full host state exchange baselines alongside single-edit controls.
Precise specification of experimental artifacts, including exact Hugging Face model commit SHAs, block layer indices, and execution runtimes.
Well-designed 2x2 factorial evaluation structure ensuring non-overlapping operand and outcome tokens across 512 held-out task instances.
weaknesses: Highly constrained domain limited to single-digit addition and subtraction with strict four-logit completion boundaries, limiting generalizability to arbitrary mathematical reasoning.
Lacks exploration of scaling beyond two operands or into multi-token output generation.
The 7x7 linear projection map is reused from an earlier single-operand setup without comparative evaluation against alternative cross-layer mapping dimensions or techniques.
suggestions: Extend the benchmark to multi-digit arithmetic and chained operations (three or more operands) to evaluate composition limits.
Provide an ablation on the projection rank (varying the 7-dimensional subspace) to determine sensitivity to subspace capacity.
Test cross-model transfer across disparate model families beyond the Qwen 2.5 architecture series.

claims.text: The both-operand arm's mean target margin was +4.07, versus +4.09 for the full host exchange and −4.74 for the random edits.
